literature_notes: Two ledger lines were evaluated, both from PMC13170660. L1 describes a myc-tag that is 'co-expressed' as a separate transfection efficiency control alongside the untagged IgLON5 construct — the myc is on a different protein, not inserted into IgLON5, so no tag insertion into IgLON5 is reported. L2 references a commercial OriGene plasmid (#225495) described as 'Myc-DKK-tagged human IgLON5', but the tag position (junction residue) is entirely unstated in the ledger; the explicit exclusion rule disqualifies commercial plasmids with unstated tag positions because insert_after_residue cannot be pinned. IgLON5 is a GPI-anchored protein (topology: signal peptide 1–30, fully extracellular 31–336, no TM or intracellular residues), so in principle an N-terminal tag after the signal peptide cleavage site (after residue 30) would be the natural surface-accessible junction, but no ledger line supports this with a stated position. Zero sites qualify.
